news.title: Infantino attendance uncertain as Fifa U-20 Women’s World Cup opens in Poland
news.lede: Fifa could not confirm by Friday whether Gianni Infantino would attend Saturday's opening matches. (EPA Images pic) KATOWICE: Some 15,000 people are expected for the opening matches of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup on Saturday, but it is not yet clear whether Fifa President Gianni Infantino will be among them. The tournament, which runs until Sept 27 in Poland, is the first major Fifa competition that could have been affected by the governance standoff that followed Infantino's proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. Infantino abandoned the proposal on July 31 after fierce opposition from Uefa and other stakeholders.

news.title: European football's safety and security community strengthens cooperation ahead of new season
news.lede: Clubs, national associations, supporter representatives and public authorities gathered in Madrid to strengthen partnerships and help deliver safe, secure and welcoming UEFA competition matches throughout the 2026/27 season. Ahead of the 2026/27 UEFA club competition season kick-off next week, representatives from across the European football community gathered in Madrid, host city for the 2027 UEFA Champions League final, to strengthen cooperation and prepare for the safety and security challenges associated with hosting European football and welcoming travelling supporters. Under this year’s "Make It Count" banner, the latest UEFA Safety and Security Conference encouraged participants to make the most of every interaction, partnership and information exchange.

news.title: Gianni Infantino attendance uncertain as FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup opens in Poland
news.lede: President of FIFA Gianni Infantino has faced calls to resign from UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF. KATOWICE – Some 15,000 people are expected for the opening matches of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup on Sept 5, but it is not yet clear whether FIFA President Gianni Infantino will be among them. The tournament, which runs until Sept 27 in Poland, is the first major FIFA competition that could have been affected by the governance stand-off that followed Infantino’s proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. Infantino abandoned the proposal on July 31 after fierce opposition from UEFA and other stakeholders.

news.title: Carlos Queiroz reappointed Ghana head coach less than two months after FIFA World Cup exit
news.lede: Accra [Ghana], September 4 (ANI): Carlos Queiroz has been reappointed as Ghana's head coach less than two months after appearing to step down from the role following the Black Stars' exit from the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the Ghana Football Association (GFA) confirmed on Thursday. According to Reuters, the 73-year-old Portuguese will return to the post during the upcoming international window after agreeing to a new coaching mandate with the GFA and Ghana's Ministry of Sports and Recreation.
